snapshot_consistency.title: A topology event invalidates the old study context
snapshot_consistency.caption: Illustrative two-feeder topology, not an electrical solution. Switch S is closed in snapshot v42 at 14:35, opens at 15:02, and produces state v43. The 14:40 study used v42. At 15:05, the operator must revalidate its applicability to v43 before relying on it.

executed_trace.title: A typed stale-data result changes the next action
executed_trace.caption: Illustrative execution trace with concrete arguments and typed results. Asset resolution returns id 447. The measurement service returns quality STALE for the requested 15:00–15:05 window. The supported continuation requests fresh data. A solver call using this unresolved stale response has no evidence basis.
executed_trace.assumptions: This is a simulated teaching trace, not a live product log or a claim that these APIs were executed against a utility.

typed_contract.title: A valid number can still violate the tool contract
typed_contract.caption: Illustrative typed contract. A solver expecting per-unit voltage and topology v43 rejects 12.47 kV and v42. A request with voltage 1.00 pu on base 12.47 kV and topology v43 can pass those checks. Unit conversion requires an explicit, matching voltage base and convention. Topology consistency is a separate requirement.
typed_contract.assumptions: The 12.47 kV example only illustrates unit normalization on the same voltage basis. It is not an electrical feasibility check or a full sufficient solver contract.

trust_boundary.title: Retrieved instructions cannot acquire command authority
trust_boundary.caption: Illustrative prompt-injection mechanism. A retrieved document contains an instruction to ignore limits and execute. Its contents remain data for retrieval and proposal formation. An independent policy and permission gate stands before the command service. The direct path from document text to command execution is blocked.
trust_boundary.assumptions: The malicious text is a teaching example, not an instruction to the presenter or an operational command. The diagram specifies an intended boundary, not proof that a system enforces it.

cache_key_failure.title: An omitted perturbation makes the retry ineffective
cache_key_failure.caption: Schematic teaching reconstruction of the reactive-load cache defect reported in R02. A first call at P=100 MW, Q=0 Mvar caches R0. A corrected call at Q=10 Mvar maps to the same schematic key because Q is omitted, so it returns R0 rather than evaluating the corrected request. key(grid,P) is illustrative, not the implementation's actual API or complete cache key. A corrective cache identity must cover topology, model, all perturbations, and other relevant solver configuration.
cache_key_failure.assumptions: Invented key notation and R0 label illustrate the reported omitted-Q mechanism. No solver result or power-flow solution is invented.

power_fault_dag.title: A fault-record DAG follows the data prerequisites
power_fault_dag.caption: Original teaching adaptation of DrAgent's domain tools, not its measured execution trace. A frozen COMTRADE record R17 feeds independent find_fault_inception and find_max_fault_current computations (abbreviated in the drawing). The inception sample and sampling rate feed a time conversion; the report waits for both numerical results.
power_fault_dag.assumptions: R17 is an invented identifier; no waveform or numerical result is invented. The simple n_f/f_s conversion assumes constant sampling rate and a zero-based index relative to record start. Production conversion must respect actual COMTRADE timestamps, indexing and rate changes. Parallel scheduling is a teaching adaptation, not a claim that the paper ran these tools concurrently.

power_stateful_route.title: A stateful graph routes the next step using validation
power_stateful_route.caption: Original LangGraph educational pattern. A plan invokes a power-flow tool and validates its returned evidence. Valid evidence finishes; invalid evidence with retries left decrements the counter and replans; exhausted retries escalate. Two retries are an explicit application policy, not a LangGraph default.
power_stateful_route.assumptions: Illustrative tool run_pf(F12,v43), state fields and budget. No tool is executed. Routing checks tool status, evidence and domain acceptance criteria; a completed graph alone does not establish electrical feasibility.
power_stateful_route.credit: Original editable TikZ teaching diagram; see caption for source and assumptions

power_checkpoint_revalidation.title: A checkpoint preserves execution state, not evidence freshness
power_checkpoint_revalidation.caption: Original educational checkpoint/resume example. A checkpoint stores execution state and solver evidence for topology v42. A topology event creates v43 during the pause. On resume, an explicit application check compares the evidence context with the current topology and recomputes affected evidence before reuse.
power_checkpoint_revalidation.assumptions: Topology versions and event are invented. Persistence does not automatically refresh solver evidence or validate domain assumptions. The diagram shows one mismatch branch; an unchanged context could pass a separately defined reuse check.
power_checkpoint_revalidation.credit: Original editable TikZ teaching diagram; see caption for source and assumptions

power_contingency_join.title: A contingency join preserves missing results
power_contingency_join.caption: Original teaching fan-out/fan-in pattern. Cases C1, C2 and C3 start from separate copies of the same frozen network v43. C2 returns a tool error. The join retains all case statuses and produces an INCOMPLETE report rather than treating the two completed cases as complete contingency coverage.
power_contingency_join.assumptions: Invented case identifiers and statuses; no power-flow measurements or contingency ranking is claimed. Independent copies prevent branch mutations from leaking between cases. Completion is distinct from a pass against operating limits.
power_contingency_join.credit: Original editable TikZ teaching diagram; see caption for source and assumptions

power_gridmind_invalidation.title: A changed input determines the stages that rerun
power_gridmind_invalidation.caption: Original affected-stage diagram derived from GridMind 2026 Table 1, PDF p.4. Changing cascade fan-out k from 50 to 200 reruns cascade only. Shifting forecast initialization by six hours reruns all five stages: line-wind, outages, ACOPF, contingency and cascade. These are reported dependency effects, not a newly executed workflow.
power_gridmind_invalidation.assumptions: The diagram shows affected sets, not invented stage-to-stage edges. In this implementation contingency consumes the outage schedule directly, not the ACOPF result. Reuse requires matching declared inputs; an artifact hash does not prove numerical correctness or freshness beyond those inputs.
power_gridmind_invalidation.credit: Original editable TikZ teaching diagram; see caption for source and assumptions

revision_agent_roles.title: The agent chooses; the tool executes a capability
revision_agent_roles.caption: Original teaching abstraction for diagnosing a frozen base case v43. An LLM agent chooses a tool call, the callable interface runs against the case and solver, and returned evidence informs the next choice. LangGraph is shown as a possible orchestration runtime for state and execution, not as a grid solver or a claim about a particular PowerAgent implementation.
revision_agent_roles.assumptions: The v43 case, run_pf(v43, base) interface and feedback fields are illustrative; no tool was executed and no numerical outcome is asserted. Tool and agent name interface/decision roles; a tool may internally wrap another agent or a complex service. The outer framework marker does not establish the correctness of any electrical result. No PowerAgent SDK relationship is claimed.
revision_agent_roles.source_locator: Russell/Norvig Section 2.1; Anthropic 'What are agents?' and 'Agents'; official LangGraph overview and Tools opening definitions.
revision_agent_roles.credit: Original native TikZ educational diagram; source and assumptions in caption

revision_powerdag_gate.title: Check the prerequisite before executing a state-dependent tool
revision_powerdag_gate.caption: Original teaching adaptation of PowerDAG v4, Section IV-C, PDF p.5. A planner proposes a voltage-violation check. A prerequisite gate blocks execution and returns the missing solve to the planner when the required solved network state is unavailable; otherwise the check proceeds. This is neither exact source code nor the complete/minimal workflow DAG.
revision_powerdag_gate.assumptions: The v43 identifier and call wording are illustrative. The figure strengthens the teaching condition to a solution for the current named network. The paper's formal supervisor tests required Write-tool names against executed-tool names; do not infer from that alone a version-aware freshness/invalidation guarantee. Rule coverage is curated rather than exhaustive, and unruled tools remain executable. A blocked call leaves environment state unchanged; passing this prerequisite is not a numerical feasibility or safety proof.
revision_powerdag_gate.source_locator: Section IV-C, PDF p.5, voltage-violation example and Eqs. (8)-(10); Algorithm 1. Figure 2, PDF p.3, locates the supervisor between planner and executor.
revision_powerdag_gate.credit: Original native TikZ educational diagram; source and assumptions in caption

va_classical_agent.caption: Original grid-study illustration of the classical observation/action abstraction. A software environment supplies case files and solver logs; an agent selects study actions or asks for evidence. The agent need not be an LLM.

va_authority.caption: Original advisory-study example. The agent performs allowed studies and returns evidence for operator review. In this explicitly defined process, only the authorized operator approves an operating action; review may instead require revision or a stop.
va_authority.assumptions: An illustrative allocation of authority, not a universal claim about every automation system or a representation of a particular utility's switching procedure. No live action is executed.

va_three_graphs.caption: Original schematics: undirected physical equipment connections, directed calculation prerequisites with fork/join dependencies, and runtime execution routes with a retry cycle. The physical network and all labels are illustrative; the diagrams are not a minimal DAG or a measured paper trace.
va_three_graphs.assumptions: Physical edges describe connectivity, not instruction order. Task edges describe required outputs, not transmission lines. Runtime edges route execution; an execution cycle and an acyclic dependency graph can describe different views of the same application.

va_powerwf.title: One PowerWF grid-impact study
va_powerwf.caption: Teaching diagram of the author-maintained PowerWF Grid Impact Evaluation example. LangGraph stores the study state; the analysis steps request PowerWorld tools. Baseline and added-load studies run in the documented order.

va_dragent.title: DrAgent plans calls to domain tools
va_dragent.caption: Teaching view of DrAgent: the plan selects tools for the question. Recorded-signal tools supply measurements; manual search supplies product information. The manual path is needed only for relevant questions.

va_simulation_feedback.caption: Simplified study-generation workflow from Jia, Cui and Hug. Execution errors return to retrieval and code repair. A run without a software error still needs a check against the requested study settings.

va_mcp.title: MCP is the connection to a callable tool
va_mcp.caption: Original teaching view of the MCP client/server connection. The application chooses a call, the client sends it to a server, and the server invokes the allowed capability. The returned result is evidence for the next step.
va_mcp.assumptions: This is a conceptual interface diagram, not a network-security guarantee or one application’s exact deployment. The application must still check permissions, arguments, case versions and the meaning of returned results.

reliability_chain.title: Small per-step error compounds across a workflow
reliability_chain.caption: Illustrative calculation: if every step has identical success probability q and steps are independent, all L required steps succeed with probability q^L. These are mathematical scenarios, not measured agent reliability. Correlated errors or unequal steps require a different model.
reliability_chain.assumptions: Identical independent Bernoulli step outcomes. All required steps must succeed.
reliability_chain.credit: Original illustrative calculation for this tutorial; not measured agent performance

zero_failure_bound.title: Zero observed failures still leaves a nonzero upper bound
zero_failure_bound.caption: Exact one-sided 95% binomial upper confidence bound after zero failures: p_upper = 1 - 0.05^(1/n). At n=30 the bound is 9.503%, at n=60 it is 4.8703%, at n=300 it is 0.9936%, and at n=3000 it is 0.09981%. It describes uncertainty under independent, identically distributed trials with a fixed failure definition and stable operating conditions. It does not establish reliability under a new topology or a new task distribution.
zero_failure_bound.assumptions: IID binomial trials, zero observed failures, prespecified one-sided 95% confidence procedure. This bound is calculated, not author-reported.
zero_failure_bound.credit: Original illustrative calculation for this tutorial; not measured agent performance

eval_outcomes.title: Conditional failure rates depend on the relevant denominator
eval_outcomes.caption: Hypothetical evaluation of 100 cases, not measured system performance. Of 80 truly feasible cases, 70 are accepted and 10 rejected. Of 20 truly infeasible cases, 2 are accepted and 18 rejected. False approval among infeasible cases is 2/20=10%, while the pooled fraction is 2/100=2%. Accepted-case precision is 70/72=97.22%. The denominator answers a different question in each metric.
eval_outcomes.assumptions: Illustrative labels and outcomes, fixed failure definition. No measured agent data.
eval_outcomes.credit: Original illustrative calculation for this tutorial; not measured agent performance

r02_capability.title: Ten attempts give a narrow evidence base
r02_capability.caption: Derived from R02 Table II, PDF page 4, tested development snapshot. Bars reproduce the eight reported 100/1000-bus count cells. Whiskers are calculated two-sided Wilson 95% intervals, not author-reported uncertainty. Their probabilistic interpretation requires comparable independent Bernoulli attempts, which the paper does not establish. The OpenAI table label is gpt 5.4 B. Larger grids and levels L3–L6 have no quantified result cells and are omitted, not encoded as zero. This is not field-deployment reliability or a current vendor ranking.
r02_capability.assumptions: Reported counts preserved. Wilson intervals conditional on independent comparable trials. Model/backend and task snapshot specific.
r02_capability.credit: Original plot derived from cited paper data; see caption for interpretation

r01_coverage.title: A successful solver call does not imply complete contingency discovery
r01_coverage.caption: Derived from R01 Table III: the four reported backend searches on one synthetic ACTIVSg200 SCOPFLOW case all found economic-critical contingency 187–189 (+21.6% cost), three identified infeasible outage 29–30, and none identified infeasible outage 15–16. These are fixed backend-run counts, not repeated IID trials, estimated probabilities, or comprehensive field reliability. No confidence interval is justified by these four heterogeneous searches.
r01_coverage.assumptions: One synthetic case, four different backend searches, reported search behavior only.
r01_coverage.credit: Original plot derived from cited paper data; see caption for interpretation

expanded_power_dynamic.title: Dynamic-model repair within a restricted action space
expanded_power_dynamic.caption: PowerAgentBench-Dyn DMQ case: ten independent sessions per model on one modified WECC solar PV dynamic model. Full-suite compliant success is 10/10 for Opus 4.8, 10/10 for Sonnet 4.6, and 9/10 for Haiku 4.5. Median updates are 1, 1 and 2. Eight quality tests and a maximum of five parameter updates define this case. No confidence interval or fleet-level performance is claimed.
expanded_power_dynamic.locator: Table II and section III-C, PDF p.3
expanded_power_dynamic.assumptions: Author-reported counts and medians reproduced, not independently rerun. One fixed corrupted model; no human or deterministic search comparator.
expanded_power_dynamic.credit: Original chart from cited author-reported research results

expanded_power_benchmark.title: Complete answers and partial credit measure different outcomes
expanded_power_benchmark.caption: Selected PowerBench Table 4 results. Macro Joint Accuracy equally weights the three task families, with 60 temporal, 90 contextual and 150 comparative questions; it is not a correct-count divided by 300. Overall Field Accuracy is the mean per-question fraction of correct fields. Whiskers are author-reported 95% bootstrap intervals, not newly calculated intervals. All three configurations used the same 300-question benchmark and 50-call/300-second retrieval-and-reasoning budgets.
expanded_power_benchmark.locator: Table 4, PDF p.8; aggregation definitions section 4.1 and Appendix D
expanded_power_benchmark.assumptions: Different aggregation rules are retained. Partial field credit is not full-task success. Do not infer pairwise significance from marginal interval overlap. Benchmark results are synthetic and author-reported; public runnable release not verified.
expanded_power_benchmark.credit: Original chart from cited author-reported scores and bootstrap intervals

expanded_power_gridmind.title: Artifact reuse saves executions and wall time
expanded_power_gridmind.caption: GridMind weather-risk workflow, same seven-query session on a synthetic Texas 2000-bus case. Full-rerun ablation executes 35 stages and takes 1432.6 s; content-addressed reuse executes 14 stages and takes 677.1 s. The stage-count reduction is 60%; the calculated wall-time speedup is 2.1158× (2.12× rounded), corresponding to 52.7363% less wall time. These are different metrics, not two descriptions of the same percentage. No repeated-session uncertainty estimate is reported.
expanded_power_gridmind.assumptions: Same reported query sequence; full-rerun arm uses fresh namespaces. Single simulation session, surrogate screening and reduced-order cascade models. No live utility operation or independently repeated performance claim.
expanded_power_gridmind.credit: Original chart from cited author-reported session/ablation measurements

power_dragent_counts.source_locator: PDF p.6 Table IV and p.8 Appendix; score definitions p.5 Table II; Q6 exception p.7 footnote 8
power_dragent_counts.caption: Correct answers (score >=2), reconstructed from Table IV and Appendix; n=18 DR cases per question. Q6 includes correctly labeled duration under footnote 8. Counts are author-data-derived, not an independent rerun.
